name: La Défense: Tour Coupole
note: Total's (Roche, Dinkeloo, 1985): dark smoked glass. A relation of stepped parts, so a restyle, keeping them. From memory.

name: La Défense: Tour Eqho
note: Ex-Descartes (2013's reclad): grey glass striped in gold at every floor (slabBands in the skyscraper-banded style; trim = the gold). A relation of parts, so a restyle.

name: Hôpital Bichat-Claude-Bernard
note: The 1980 tower on its podium: pale precast panels and dark ribbons of window (a street photograph, 48.8995 2.3328). A relation of parts, so a restyle.

name: Hôpital Sainte-Anne: the pavilions
note: Questel's asylum (1867): the two long low ranges, stone under slate on a garden plan; the bake's 5–11 m is short of their three floors. The taller blocks about them are 20th-century and stay generic. Tones from memory; street-view check listed.

name: Hôpital Saint-Antoine: the wards
note: The 12th's hospital, rebuilt from the 1960s on: pale blocks. From memory; street-view check listed. Caroli, Robert André, the Horloge and Foulques de Neuilly stay parisCivic.

name: Hôpital Saint-Joseph
note: Rebuilt in the 2000s behind the Rue Raymond-Losserand: pale cladding and glass. From memory; street-view check listed.

name: Institut Curie: the hospital
note: Rue d'Ulm's hospital blocks, 1960s to Bâtiment Constant Burg's 2010s. The Pavillon du Radium is a small stone house across the garden, left to the kit.

name: Ancien hôpital Beaujon
note: The Faubourg-Saint-Honoré's (Girardin, 1784), in the 8th: a cream front whatever its age (owner's rule, 2026-10-31). The Beaujon of today is at Clichy, past the box.

name: Institut Pasteur: the original institute
note: Brébant's institute (1888), inaugurated by Sadi Carnot: pale stone panelled in red brick, slate mansards (a street photograph, 48.8408 2.3112; aerial 48.8405 2.3112). The brick is the trim here.

name: Institut Pasteur: Centre François Jacob
note: The modern labs on the Rue du Docteur-Roux's other side. From memory.

name: Université Paris Cité: the Faculté de médecine
note: 45 Rue des Saints-Pères (Madeline, 1937–53), filling a block of the 6th: a great cream stone cliff with long ranks of tall windows and a flat top (owner's rule: the 6th is cream).

name: Institut d'Art et d'Archéologie
note: batch7/institutes.ts: Bigot, 1928. Red brick and its frieze: was parisCivic.

name: Institut Océanographique de Paris
note: batch7/institutes.ts: Nénot, 1911. Was parisCivic.

name: L'Ircam: the tower
note: Standalone at the Bains-Douches's north-east corner, read off the aerial 48.8597 2.3510; the exact corner is worth a street-view check.
